correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, root size L is uniform and the two extreme depths are independent given L; their conditional laws are opposite monotone functions of L. The reversed Chebyshev identity gives strict covariance of all nonconstant increasing transforms. Independent record indicators give marginal mean/variance; binomial coefficient differentiation produces exact mixed moment and covariance 1-H_n^(2); triangular-array CLT for central root splits plus negligible tails establishes joint independence after sqrt(log n) scaling. A separate exact checker passed 796 assertions, including all n! insertions through n=8 and recurrence/harmonic identities to n=300. Infinite claims rest on the analytic proof.

evidence: Seidel–Aragon develops randomized search trees and per-key depth expectations rather than the specified pair of extreme ranks.
Devroye–Neininger studies distances, finger search, fixed ranks and normal limits; those results do not determine the strict bivariate quadrant inequality from marginal laws.
Panholzer–Prodinger studies spans of randomly selected nodes. Random node selection does not imply results for the deterministic pair of smallest/largest nodes.

originality.rationale: The fixed pair of smallest/largest key depths, its strict negative quadrant ordering, exact mixed covariance and bivariate normal limit are not given in the inspected relevant primary statements; prior one-key record laws and selected-key distance results do not imply the joint ordering. Implicit coverage by general multivariate search-tree analyses remains a named risk.
residual_risks: A general multivariate random-treap path formula not inspected here could imply the strict negative quadrant order.
A specialized historical comparison of deterministic leftmost/rightmost search depths could predate the present proof.
The algebraic identity for harmonic sums is classical; novelty is claimed for the coupled extremal-depth conclusions, not that identity.

value.rationale: The two extreme-key access depths are basic boundary costs in sorted search structures. Strict negative quadrant dependence provides inequalities for every increasing cost/penalty transform; the exact covariance is finite, strictly decreasing and nonzero asymptotically even as standardized depths approach independent Gaussian limits. This strong dependence-ordering/limit contrast has structural motivation beyond a routine marginal moment computation.
